feed.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories
feed.subtitle: Top stories in the U.S. and world news, politics, health, science, business, music, arts and culture. Nonprofit journalism with a mission. This is NPR.

entry.title: The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September as job market lacks spark
entry.summary: U.S. employers added 29,000 jobs in September as the unemployment rate inched up to 4.2%. Job gains for July and August were revised down by a total of 60,000 jobs, extending a lackluster run for the job market.

entry.title: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
entry.summary: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.

entry.title: Failed 'torturous' execution attempt on Christa Pike reignites death penalty debate
entry.summary: The botched execution in Tennessee of Christa Pike, who survived despite being subject to two doses of lethal injection on Wednesday, has reignited furious debate about the death penalty in the U.S.

entry.title: Discursive Verses: when pulling rank goes wrong
entry.summary: NPR Music culture critic and reporter Rodney Carmichael ruminates on the latest in rap culture. This week: a hip-hop divorce, an OutKast lawsuit and the state of rap music on the charts.

entry.title: Who uttered the phrase 'the ideological clowns are out' this week? The quiz knows
entry.summary: Plus, how well do you know your pandas and fat bears?

entry.title: The U.S. Senate is up for grabs. Can this Ohio Democrat win back working class votes?
entry.summary: After 32 years in Congress, Ohio's Sherrod Brown lost his Senate seat in 2024 as many working class voters turned out for Trump. Now Brown is counting on union voters to send him back to Washington.

entry.title: Pro-democracy activists increasingly vulnerable to authoritarian governments in Southeast Asia
entry.summary: Activists across Asia are being hunted down by authoritarian governments even across international borders. Human rights groups have been warning of a "swap market" of repression in Southeast Asia.

entry.title: After bankruptcy, he was banned from sports betting sites. Then he discovered Kalshi
entry.summary: The dark side of the prediction market boom is becoming more clear: Experts say the sites have become go-to outlets for gambling addicts to relapse as the companies avoid state consumer protections.

entry.title: 10 books we are looking forward to this fall
entry.summary: Move over, beach reads. With the fall equinox behind us, we can now curl up with cozy autumn books. There are new titles coming from Barbara Kingsolver, Chad Harbach, Jasmine Guillory and more.

entry.title: The family of Renee Good files lawsuits over her death during Minneapolis ICE raids
entry.summary: The fatal shooting of Renee Good by a federal immigration agent last January in Minneapolis set off a firestorm of protests around the U.S. Her family is speaking out for the first time.
